item.content:encoded:
Good idea, poor execution. It doesn't feel tonally like an SCP article, and there were a few things that didn't make sense to be put in there.

SCP-608 appears to be a length of silver tinsel with an unusually furry appearance.

"Appears to be"? Say it either is or is not. Granted I've fallen prey to this as well, but try to avoid the term "appears to be" in an SCP article. I understand that it's a fractal, but try to describe it something like this:

SCP-608 is a length of silver tinsel approximately >x< centimeters long and >y< centimeters in diameter.

You could probably continue from there. Another thing, after explaining that the object is a fractal, you explain fractals "in layman's terms". The foundation are professionals, and expect the people reading these articles to know what everything means. Beyond that, the actual readers aren't idiots. We have Google.

Downvoted for now, but fix the tone and it may change.

item.content:encoded:
Overall, I liked this concept. It is intriguing and interesting. I had to downvote it, however, for two reasons. First off, there is a considerable amount of technological lingo (aka technobabble) that I just wasn't able to follow. Try to tone it down some, or just go into a more detailed explanation of what it means using simpler terms. TL;DR: Dumb it down.

My second issue, which will be harder to fix, is that the tone is just all wrong. You have this written more like a narrative; if you want to discuss the history of the object, add a "discovery" section. As well, talking about how a new researcher came and saved the day is just a bit silly and superfluous. The description should only be information that someone new to the object would need to handle it effectively.

So yeah, overall I liked it but downvoted for the aforementioned reasons. If you can fix those up I may switch my vote. Good luck!
